data.name: ZwiftConnected

data.comment: Connections screen, your controller card, when a controller is connected. {0} is the controller name, for example Xbox Series X Controller.

data.name: ConnectionsControllerAwake
data.comment: Connections screen, second line under the controller name when a controller is connected.

data.name: ConnectionsNoController
data.comment: Connections screen, your controller card, when no controller is connected. It asks the person to press a button on the controller to wake it.

data.name: ConnectionsLooking
data.comment: Connections screen, second line when no controller is connected. The app is still scanning for one.

data.name: ConnectionsPickerLabel
data.comment: Connections screen, label of the dropdown that switches to another connected controller.

data.name: ConnectionsPairBluetooth
data.comment: Connections screen, button that opens the Windows Bluetooth settings so the person can pair a controller.

data.name: ConnectionsShowMeHow
data.comment: Connections screen, button on the Zwift card that shows the three steps to pair with Zwift again.

data.name: ConnectionsHideSteps
data.comment: Connections screen, button on the Zwift card that hides the three steps to pair with Zwift. It replaces Show me how while the steps are open.

data.name: ConnectionsTrainerReminder
data.value: Set Power Source back to your trainer in Zwift.
data.comment: Connections screen, reminder under the Zwift status while Zwift is connected. Power Source is the Zwift setting that picks the trainer.

data.name: ZwiftStepPowerSource
data.comment: Zwift step 1, with its number. In Zwift, the person sets the Power Source device to Voltage Gamepad. Keep Power Source and Voltage Gamepad as they appear in Zwift.

data.name: ZwiftStepControls
data.comment: Zwift step 2, with its number. In Zwift, the person sets the Controls device to Voltage Gamepad. Keep Controls and Voltage Gamepad as they appear in Zwift.

data.name: ZwiftStepTrainer
data.comment: Zwift step 3, with its number. In Zwift, the person sets the Power Source device back to their trainer. Keep Power Source as it appears in Zwift.

data.name: SettingsTitle
data.comment: Title of the Settings screen.

data.name: SettingsAppearanceSection
data.comment: Heading of the section on the Settings screen where the person picks Light, Dark, or Match Windows.

data.name: SettingsRidesSection
data.comment: Heading of the section on the Settings screen about rides, which start and end by themselves.

data.name: SettingsRideTimeout
data.comment: Label of the number box on the Settings screen. The number is minutes, and a ride ends after that many minutes without a button press or without a connection.

data.name: SettingsRideTimeoutDescription
data.value: Minutes without a button press or a connection before a ride ends. The minimum is 5.
data.comment: Description under the ride timeout number box on the Settings screen.

data.name: SettingsRideTimeoutMinimum
data.value: The ride timeout must be 5 minutes or more.
data.comment: Message on the Settings screen shown when the person types a ride timeout below 5 minutes.

data.name: SettingsMappingsSection
data.comment: Heading of the section on the Settings screen about saved mappings. A mapping is a saved set of button assignments for one controller.

data.name: SettingsOpenMappings
data.comment: Button on the Settings screen that opens the folder where saved mappings are kept, so the person can copy files to share them.

data.name: SettingsDeleteAll
data.comment: Button on the Settings screen that deletes every saved mapping after asking.

data.name: SettingsDeleteAllConfirmOne
data.value: Delete 1 saved mapping? This can't be undone. Default stays.
data.comment: Confirmation on the Settings screen when exactly one mapping is saved. Default is the built-in mapping that cannot be deleted.

data.name: SettingsDeleteAllConfirm
data.value: Delete all {0} saved mappings? This can't be undone. Default stays.
data.comment: Confirmation on the Settings screen when more than one mapping is saved. {0} is how many. Default is the built-in mapping that cannot be deleted.

data.name: SettingsDeleteNone
data.value: There are no saved mappings to delete.
data.comment: Description shown under the disabled Delete all saved mappings button on the Settings screen when no mapping is saved.

data.name: SettingsDeleteConfirmTitle
data.comment: Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting every saved mapping.

data.name: SettingsDeleteConfirmButton
data.comment: Confirm button of the dialog for deleting every saved mapping.

data.comment: Link on the Settings screen to the Help and feedback screen.

data.comment: Heading of the section on the Settings screen with the app version and the link to Credits.

data.name: SettingsVersionFormat
data.comment: Line on the Settings screen that shows the app version. {0} is the version number, for example 0.6.0.

data.name: SettingsCreditsLinkText
data.comment: Link on the Settings screen to the Credits screen.

data.name: AppName
data.comment: The name of the app. Keep Zwift, which is a product name.

data.name: CreditsTitle
data.comment: Title of the Credits screen.

data.name: CreditsVersionFormat
data.comment: Line on the Credits screen that shows the app version. {0} is the version number, for example 0.6.0.

data.name: CreditsDescription
data.value: Use the controller you already own to shift and steer in Zwift. Free and open source, with no ads and no account.
data.comment: Short description of the app on the Credits screen.

data.name: CreditsNotAffiliated
data.value: Not made by or affiliated with Zwift. Zwift and Zwift Ride are trademarks of Zwift, Inc.
data.comment: Disclaimer on the Credits screen. Keep Zwift and Zwift Ride, which are product names.

data.name: CreditsGitHub
data.comment: Link on the Credits screen that opens the project's GitHub page. Keep GitHub, which is a product name.

data.name: CreditsGitHubDescription
data.comment: Description under the Project on GitHub link on the Credits screen.

data.name: CreditsList
data.comment: Row label on the Credits screen that opens the list of projects and people the app builds on. Also the title of that list screen.

data.name: CreditsListDescription
data.value: The projects and people this builds on
data.comment: Description under the Credits row on the Credits screen.

data.name: CreditsLicenseName
data.comment: Row label on the Credits screen that opens the license text. Also the title of that screen.

data.name: CreditsLicenseValue
data.comment: Description under the License row on the Credits screen. The name of a software license.

data.name: SupportTitle
data.comment: Title of the Support this project screen.

data.name: SupportPitch
data.value: This app is free and open source, with no ads and no account. If it's earned a place in your rides, you can chip in.
data.comment: Short pitch at the top of the Support this project screen.

data.name: SupportKofi
data.comment: Button on the Support this project screen that opens the project's Ko-fi page. Keep Ko-fi, which is a product name.

data.name: SupportOtherWays
data.comment: Heading above the quieter ways to help on the Support this project screen.

data.name: SupportStar
data.comment: Row label on the Support this project screen that opens the project's GitHub page so the person can star it. Keep GitHub.

data.name: SupportStarDescription
data.comment: Description under the Star it on GitHub row.

data.name: SupportShare
data.comment: Row label on the Support this project screen that copies a link to the project.

data.name: SupportShareDescription
data.comment: Description under the Tell a friend row.

data.name: SupportShareCopied
data.comment: Status on the Support this project screen after the link was copied to the clipboard. Read out by screen readers.

data.name: SupportContribute
data.value: Help with the code or docs
data.comment: Row label on the Support this project screen that opens the contributing guide.

data.name: SupportContributeDescription
data.comment: Description under the Help with the code or docs row. Keep GitHub.

data.name: RideControllerHere
data.comment: Ride screen, controller card, when a controller is connected. {0} is the controller name, for example Xbox Controller.

data.name: RideNoControllerTitle
data.comment: Title of the Ride screen when no controller is connected. It asks the person to press a button on the controller to wake it.

data.name: RideNoControllerStatus
data.comment: Ride screen status while the app looks for a controller.

data.name: RidePairWithZwift
data.comment: Main button on the Ride screen when Zwift is not connected. It opens the Connections tab, which has the pairing steps. Keep Zwift.

data.name: RideMappingLabel
data.comment: Label on the Ride screen above the name of the selected mapping. A mapping is a saved set of button assignments.

data.name: RideChangeMapping
data.comment: Button on the Ride screen that opens the Buttons tab so the person can pick another mapping.

data.name: RideWordmarkName
data.comment: Screen reader name of the VOLTAGE wordmark at the top of the Ride screen. VOLTAGE is a brand name and stays as it is.

data.name: RideStatsRidesOne
data.comment: Ride screen stat, shown when exactly one ride has been counted.

data.name: RideStatsRidesOther
data.comment: Ride screen stat. {0} is how many rides have been counted, two or more.

data.name: RideStatsShiftsOne
data.comment: Ride screen stat, shown when exactly one shift has been counted.

data.name: RideStatsShiftsOther
data.comment: Ride screen stat. {0} is how many shifts have been counted, zero or two or more.

data.name: RideStatsSince
data.comment: Ride screen stat. {0} is the month and year of the first counted ride, for example September 2026.

data.name: RideJustPressed
data.comment: Small label above the big readout of the last button press on the Ride screen while riding.

data.name: RidePressFormat
data.comment: Big readout of the last button press while riding. {0} is what the button does, for example Shift up, and {1} is the button, for example right bumper.

data.name: RideNoPress
data.comment: Big readout while riding before any button was pressed.

data.name: RideShiftsThisRide
data.comment: Line while riding. {0} is the number of shifts so far.

data.name: RideQuickReference
data.comment: Heading above the shift buttons while riding.

data.name: RideQuickReferenceFormat
data.comment: Quick reference line while riding. {0} is the button, for example Right bumper, and {1} is what it does, for example Shift up.

data.name: RideZwiftLostTitle
data.comment: Title on the Ride screen while riding when Zwift lost the connection. It tells the person the controller is not the problem.

data.name: RideZwiftLostBody
data.value: Pick Voltage Gamepad under Controls in Zwift again.
data.comment: Instruction on the Ride screen when Zwift lost the connection. Keep Voltage Gamepad, which is the device name Zwift shows, and keep Controls and Zwift.

data.name: RideControllerAsleepTitle
data.comment: Title on the Ride screen while riding when the controller disconnected, for example because it went to sleep or was turned off.

data.name: RideControllerAsleepBody
data.value: Wake it up to reconnect and continue riding.
data.comment: Instruction on the Ride screen when the controller disconnected. It asks the person to wake the controller so it reconnects.

data.name: RideControllerBack
data.comment: Status on the Ride screen, read out by screen readers, when the controller returned during a ride.

data.name: RideFinishedTitle
data.comment: Title of the summary that shows when a ride ends.

data.name: RideFinishedTime
data.comment: Line in the ride summary. {0} is the length of the ride, for example 1 h 5 min.

data.name: RideFinishedShifts
data.comment: Line in the ride summary. {0} is the number of shifts.

data.name: RideFinishedRides
data.comment: Line in the ride summary. {0} is how many rides have been counted in total.

data.name: RideDurationHoursMinutes
data.comment: Length of a ride of an hour or more. {0} is hours and {1} is minutes.

data.name: RideDurationMinutes
data.comment: Length of a ride under an hour. {0} is minutes.

data.name: RideFinishedDone
data.comment: Button on the ride summary that returns to the Ride screen.

data.name: RideAskPitch
data.value: This app is free. If it's earned a place in your rides, you can support the project.
data.comment: One-time message on the ride summary that asks for support. It does not claim any result.

data.name: RideAskLater
data.comment: Button on the one-time support message that dismisses it. The message does not come back.
